passage:
Counsellor's note, after the parent visit on Wednesday. Anand, a father, came in worried about how to tell his nine-year-old, Bela, that Nani was very ill and that the family would be visiting the hospital often. I sat in while he told her at the school bench. He did not say Nani was "resting". He said, "Nani is very sick. The doctors are working hard to help her. Nobody caused it, and it's okay to be sad. You can ask me anything."
Bela was quiet, then asked, "Will she come home?" Anand said, "We don't know yet, and I will tell you what I know." Bela leaned against his arm.
Sarika, school counsellor

qa.q: What might Bela have been feeling when asking "Will she come home?"
qa.a: Bela was probably scared and wanted to know the truth. Leaning against Anand's arm shows a need for closeness.

qa.q: What did Anand do that helped Bela trust him?
qa.a: Anand used plain words, said Nobody caused it and invited questions. When he did not know the answer, he said so instead of hiding it.

qa.q: How might Anand have felt while telling Bela about Nani?
qa.a: Anand was probably worried and sad, and also determined to be honest. Coming in for support beforehand shows how hard it was.

grounding: A parent tells a child in simple terms why a relative is ill, and honesty at the child's level builds trust.

passage:
Sunday night. Told Parul, my nine-year-old, about the move today. I was dreading it. I sat on her bed and said, "Parul, my new job is in another city. We are moving in June. You will go to a new school." I did not say "it will be fun, don't worry." I said I was a little scared too.
She cried. Then she asked, "Will I have to leave my best friend Meghna?" I said yes, and that Meghna and she can call every Sunday. She asked about her room, her books, the cat. I answered each question, even the ones I didn't know: "I'll find out."
She fell asleep holding my hand. I felt tired and lighter.
— Amandeep

qa.q: When are Amandeep and Parul moving?
What was Amandeep feeling before telling Parul about the move?
qa.a: Amandeep was dreading it and felt a little scared. Saying "I was dreading it" and admitting the fear to Parul show honest nerves.

qa.q: What did Amandeep do that gave Parul the truth without overwhelming her?
qa.a: Amandeep gave plain facts, said it was a little scary too and answered each question, even saying "I'll find out". No cheerful cover story was offered.

qa.q: What might Parul have felt when asking "Will I have to leave my best friend Meghna?"
qa.a: Parul was probably sad and worried about losing a friend. Hearing that they could call every Sunday gave some comfort.

grounding: A person tells their nine-year-old plainly why the family is moving, answering questions honestly at the child's level.
